sections.name: Why Barber Poles Are Red and White

lines.prompt: A classic red, white and blue striped barber pole spinning outside a modern barbershop at dusk, warm window glow

lines: Ever wondered why barber poles have red and white stripes? It's a pretty dark story.

lines.prompt: A medieval barber shop interior, a barber cutting a man's hair while another customer waits with his arm bandaged

lines: For centuries, barbers didn't just cut hair. They pulled teeth, set bones, and did surgery.

lines.prompt: A medieval barber-surgeon holding a patient's arm over a brass bowl, the patient gripping a wooden pole

lines: Their most common job was bloodletting. The patient squeezed a pole to make their veins stand out.

lines.prompt: White linen bandages hanging out to dry on a wooden pole outside a medieval shop in the wind

lines: Afterwards, so the story goes, the bandages were washed and hung outside on that pole to dry.

lines.prompt: The bandages twisting around the pole in the wind forming a spiral, sunset light

lines: As they twisted in the wind, they formed a spiral. Red and white.

lines.prompt: A medieval barber shop sign transforming into a painted red and white striped pole, a barber proudly polishing it

lines: That spiral became the barber's sign. The blue stripe was added later, in America.
